content: The University of the West of England (UWE), often pronounced you-we, is a higher education institution located in Bristol, England. Its primary campus is situated in Frenchay, approximately 7 kilometers north of Bristol's city center. Additional campuses include St Matthias, the Faculty of Health and Social Care at Glenside in northeast Bristol, and the Bristol School of Art, Media, and Design at Bower Ashton, near Ashton Court in southwest Bristol. UWE also operates regional centers in Bath and Swindon, as well as an associate faculty in Hartpury, Gloucestershire, which specializes in agricultural and sports-related courses. Hartpury has hosted the European Young Rider Championship, a prestigious equestrian competition. The Bristol Old Vic Theatre School is affiliated with UWE's Faculty of Humanities, Languages, and Social Sciences. UWE is the larger of the two universities in Bristol, with approximately 30,000 students and 3,000 academic staff, compared to the University of Bristol's 23,000 students. Notably, 86% of UWE students come from state schools. The Frenchay campus houses the Bolland Library, named after Dr. Robert Bolland, the first director of Bristol Polytechnic from 1969 to 1974. The campus is conveniently located near the M32 motorway and is a 20-minute walk from Bristol Parkway railway station, which offers connections to Cardiff (30 minutes by train) and Birmingham (1 hour and 15 minutes). The Chancellor of UWE is the Rt Hon Baroness Elizabeth Butler-Sloss, GBE, and the acting Vice-Chancellor is Professor Steven West. UWE is recognized as a leading modern university and ranks highly in teaching league tables compiled by the Quality Assurance Agency. In 2006, it achieved 64th place out of 108 institutions in the good honors rankings by the Times Higher Education Supplement. UWE was established in 1970 as Bristol Polytechnic, but its origins can be traced back to the Merchant Venturers' Navigation School, founded in 1595. The institution evolved into a technical college and later merged with other colleges to form the polytechnic. It gained university status and its current name following the Further and Higher Education Act of 1992. The Bower Ashton site originated in 1969 as the West of England College of Art, previously the art school of the Royal West of England Academy. The St Matthias site was formerly a teacher training college, as was Redland College, and both became part of Bristol Polytechnic around 1976. The Avon and Gloucestershire College of Health (now the Glenside Campus) and the Bath and Swindon College of Health Studies joined UWE in 1996, followed by Hartpury in 1997. In August 2006, an £80 million student village was completed at the Frenchay campus, featuring a sports center and accommodation for 2,000 students. The university's name, The University of the West of England, Bristol, is often considered lengthy, and discussions about renaming the institution have occurred. Proposed names have included Bristol Frenchay University, Bristol Avon University, Bristol Severn University, the University of North Bristol, and the simplified University of Western England. UWE is organized into faculties, which are further divided into schools. These include the Faculty of Applied Sciences, the Bristol School of Art, Media, and Design, the Bristol Business School, the Faculty of the Built Environment, the Faculty of Computing, Engineering, and Mathematical Sciences, the Faculty of Education, the Faculty of Health and Social Care, the Faculty of Humanities, Languages, and Social Sciences, and the Faculty of Law. Each faculty encompasses specialized schools, such as the School of Biomedical Sciences, the School of Fine Arts, the School of Accounting and Finance, and the School of Civil Engineering, among others. The university's coat of arms reflects Bristol's maritime heritage and its connection to the Merchant Venturers' Navigation School. The crest features a small fleet with a ship's mast and rigging, symbolizing guidance, hope, and the pursuit of knowledge. The central shield incorporates elements from the College of St Matthias, with a wavy line representing the Avon and Severn rivers. The unicorn and sea stag, drawn from the arms of the City of Bristol and the former County of Avon, respectively, each bear a crown of King Edgar, who was crowned in Bath Abbey. The creatures also support apple trees, symbolizing the tree of knowledge, derived from the coat of arms of the Council for National Academic Awards, which previously accredited degrees awarded by Bristol Polytechnic. The motto, Light, Liberty, Learning, is a quotation from Disraeli and aligns with the symbolism of the coat of arms. The University of the West of England Students' Union (UWESU), formerly known as Bristol Polytechnic Students' Union, was established in 1971 and is based at the Frenchay campus. It is managed by four annually elected sabbatical officers. The union operates bars at all main sites, including Escape and Red at Frenchay, Bar 75 at Glenside, St Matt's Bar, and Bower Ashton Bar. Shops are also available at Frenchay, Glenside, St Matthias, and Bower Ashton. UWESU Jobs provides employment opportunities for students. At the Frenchay campus, facilities include a NatWest bank, a Blackwell's bookstore, and various dining options such as Core 24, One Zone Lounge, and Street Café. There are also coffee shops and staff-only facilities. A new sports center opened in August 2006, featuring a large hall with a wooden sprung floor, squash courts, a fitness suite, changing rooms, and all-weather pitches. The St Matthias campus offers a small sports hall and outdoor pitches. The Centre for Student Affairs provides advice, counseling, and career development services, while a multi-faith chaplaincy is based at the Octagon Centre at Frenchay. In September 2006, the Frenchay Student Village opened, providing on-campus accommodation for 1,932 students, in addition to the 252 units at Carroll Court. Accommodation is also available at the Glenside and St Matthias campuses. In partnership with UNITE Student Housing, UWE offers an additional 1,500 places in Bristol city center and assists students in finding vetted private rentals.
